The test image shows a tomato stem cut longitudinally, revealing very dark (near-black) internal discoloration of the pith/vascular tissue. The outer cortex remains greenish-white. This is a classic stem cross-section for diagnosis.

Top candidates based on the internal stem discoloration:
- **Sclerotinia_Timber_Rot**: positive ID by longitudinal stem slicing; hard grayish-black sclerotia inside stem
- **Verticillium_Wilt**: brown vascular discoloration visible when stems cut lengthwise
- **Southern_Bacterial_Wilt**: dark/light brown pith discoloration

Let me view the Sclerotinia stem reference since it's the strongest candidate (the dark material inside looks like sclerotia).

The reference Sclerotinia image shows exterior bleached stem with black sclerotia on the surface. The test image shows a stem cut longitudinally with very dark (near-black) material filling the interior pith cavity — which matches exactly the Sclerotinia description: "Hard, grayish-black sclerotia... embedded within the stem tissue; positive identification achieved by slicing the diseased stem longitudinally."

The external left portion of the cut stem also shows browning/canker consistent with Sclerotinia infection at the stem base.
